title: CMOS inverter amplifier
description: A CMOS inverter used as an analog amplifier: the input drives both an NMOS and a PMOS gate, and the two devices share one drain current stacked between the rails (current reuse). Because both transconductances act on the same input, the stage transconductance is the sum $g_{m,tot} = g_{m,n} + g_{m,p}$, so the inverter gives roughly twice the $g_m$ of a single device at the same current - the reason it is the workhorse gain cell for low-voltage, power-efficient design. The gain is $g_{m,tot}/(g_{ds,n} + g_{ds,p})$. The two gates are one node and the two sources are the two rails, so the gate-source voltages add up to the supply, $V_{GS,n} + |V_{GS,p}| = V_{DD}$: one shared gate carrying one shared current leaves a single degree of freedom between the two inversion levels, so one is a choice and the other follows from it. The sheet is drawn that way. The NMOS is sized from the bias current and its $g_m/I_D$, and its gate-source voltage is the input level $V_{in}$; the PMOS carries the NMOS's current at the gate-source voltage the supply leaves above $V_{in}$, and its width and inversion level are whatever that takes. An inverting amplifier biased by its own feedback sits at its trip point, where its input and output levels coincide, so an advisory check compares the input level the NMOS sets against the stated output level; bringing the two together is the design work this sheet exists to show. Both devices are composed children; pick the PMOS child table to the p polarity and set p_sign to -1 for a signed-PMOS axis.

params.name: V_out
params.note: output DC level; sets both devices' drain-source voltages (ideally near mid-supply). The two drains meet at a high-impedance output that nothing on this sheet holds; the feedback that biases the inverter at its trip point holds it (a resistor from output to input, or an outer loop), and with that self-bias it equals V_in

params.name: cdd_est
params.note: output-node parasitic estimate (both drains + wiring); refine from extraction

params.name: I_bias
params.note: the single current both devices carry (current reuse), typed into the NMOS at the design point; the PMOS reads the NMOS's current. Where the design is held at another condition the supply stays and this current is solved again, between min and max, so that the two devices carry one current at the gate voltage the supply leaves them

params.name: gm_id_n
params.note: NMOS inversion — the one inversion level this sheet chooses. It sets the input level, and through it the PMOS: a higher gm/ID here lowers the input level and hands the PMOS more gate-source voltage, pushing it further into strong inversion. The default puts the input level at the mid-supply output level, the trip point, on a sky130 typical-corner table; on a process with lower thresholds the same level lands lower and leaves the PMOS deeper in strong inversion

params.name: p_sign
params.note: sign convention of the PMOS table's voltage axes: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis. The PMOS's drain-source and gate-source voltages are both passed in it

doc.title: NMOS device
doc.description: The pull-down device at the shared current, drain at the output. Its current is the one this sheet types, and its inversion level is the one it chooses; its source is at ground, so its gate-source voltage is the input level. Exposes its transconductance, output conductance, saturation voltage, current, gate-source voltage, and channel-noise density.

doc.title: PMOS device
doc.description: The pull-up device at the shared current, source at VDD, drain at the output. It carries the NMOS's current (current reuse) and its gate is the NMOS's gate, so its gate-source voltage is what the supply leaves above the input level and its width is what carries that current there. Its inversion level is read off the table, not chosen. Exposes its transconductance, output conductance, saturation voltage, current, gate-source voltage and inversion level.

params.name: vgs_d
params.note: the supply down to the shared gate, signed to this table's axis convention

params.name: vds_d
params.note: source-to-drain headroom, signed to this table's axis convention

equations.name: V_in
equations.note: the input level this design sits at — the voltage on the gate the two devices share. The NMOS's source is at ground, so it is the NMOS's gate-source voltage, and the PMOS is sized at what the supply leaves above it. An OUTPUT of the NMOS's sizing, not a setting: whatever drives the input has to sit here

equations.name: V_in_p
equations.note: where the PMOS puts the same gate: its source is at VDD, so the gate sits one PMOS gate-source voltage below the supply — the gate-source voltage it was read at. abs() because a signed-PMOS table keeps that axis negative

equations.name: gm_tot
equations.note: current reuse: both devices' transconductances act on the same input and add

equations.name: gout
equations.note: both output conductances load the node

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: the resistance this stage presents at its output — both devices' output conductances in parallel. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: Av
equations.note: combined transconductance into the combined output conductance

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: both channel-noise currents (each device's own vnth_m*gm) sum and refer to the input by gm_tot

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance the input terminal presents. Both gates are driven together, so both gate capacitances load the driver. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it — and here the drain swings against the gate, so that omission is at its worst. No rule reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the single inverting branch, with both devices stacked on the one current. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

checks.note: the trip point: an inverting amplifier biased by its own feedback (a resistor from output to input) sits where its input and output levels coincide. The input level is the NMOS's gate-source voltage, set by its inversion level and length, and the output level is stated, so this compares the two, within one percent of the stated output level. Tune gm_id_n or L_n until they agree, or state the output level an outer loop holds instead

an assertion on the gate tie: the PMOS's gate, one PMOS gate-source voltage below the supply, is the input level the NMOS sets. The PMOS is handed exactly that gate-source voltage, so this holds wherever it is read there, and trips only where the two are read apart — a PMOS gate-source voltage past the table's edge, clamped to it, or a run that reads the two devices separately. Within one percent of the input level
read from the table's own noise where it carries it, and from the γ = 1 estimate otherwise; the simulator owns noise sign-off
combined gm over the total output capacitance
